correctness.rationale: Part-sign and (n-1)-dimensional opposite-sign trace inequalities give the exact universal SLEM bound. Equality forces zero trace of a positive semidefinite operator, hence every opposite-sign transverse vector is a top eigenvector. Two row/column identities then force a single edge weight via connectedness of the permissible-pair incidence graph. The stability inequality uses K^2<=2mu K, a three-step incidence diameter bound, and exact control of the total edge weight. Exact rational identities and 2577 direct numerical matrix cases were executed from the extracted package verifier; finite tests are not substituted for the general argument.

value.rationale: The full optimizer-set classification is nontrivial because convex spectral optimization permits non-invariant and nonunique optima. The stability bound provides an explicit, all-feasible-kernel identifiability guarantee for numerical near-optimal SDP outputs; this is a structural infinite-family result rather than a new number from an existing formula. Uniqueness and quantitative control are useful even though the basic optimal value has long been known.
